{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The ferry stopped running to Hallø the year the school closed, and after that the island kept its own time. Einar noticed it first in the church clock, which nobody wound anymore and which had settled at twenty past four the way a tired man settles into a chair. Then he noticed it in himself. He woke when the light woke him and ate when the gulls did, and the calendar on the wall stayed on August because August had been a good month.

There were eleven of them left. Twelve, if you counted Solveig's dog, and Solveig did. They met on Sundays in the schoolhouse because the church was too big now, the eleven of them rattling in it like dried peas in a jar. Someone read from the book. Someone made coffee. Nobody preached.

The mainland sent a boat once a month with mail and flour and a nurse who checked their blood pressure and wrote numbers on a form. She asked Einar once whether he was lonely. He thought about it honestly. He said he was not, and he was not, though he could see why she asked.

What he did not tell her was that the island had started speaking again. Not in words. In the way the moss had come back over the schoolyard, in the seals hauled up on the old ferry ramp, in the silence after the last outboard motor coughed out at evening. It was the sound of a place remembering what it had been before anyone needed it.

He did not mind being the one who heard it."}
